technology.summary:
Today's most important technology news includes Elon Musk's intensification of his attack on Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani over the Starlink India launch delay, accusing him of blocking competition. Anthropic has cut off its internal evaluations from the live internet, citing its inability to reliably control its AI agents. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman unveiled the company's new AI agent Dots at OpenAI DevDay, promising to set a new standard for privacy in frontier AI.

Other technology news includes the release of LG's RGB LED TV, the Telo MT1 electric truck, and AI-driven bird feeders. Additionally, a list of notable AI agents that can live in text messages has been compiled.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has joined forces with the Reserve Bank of India to simplify regulatory procedures for foreign portfolio investors. This comes as the Nifty index faces pressure due to global uncertainty and investor caution, with foreign portfolio investors recording net sales of Rs 10,148 crore. Indian equity benchmarks have also declined over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices, while hospital stocks have slipped following a Supreme Court of India ruling on cancer drug markups. Meanwhile, a resurgent El Niño pattern could deepen a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, pushing yields higher.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court is set to list a plea to allow peaceful protests to Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Congress party has condemned the detention of tribal students who were heading to Mumbai to protest.

In other news, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process "corrupt", citing an Indian election that did not happen. This appears to be a mix-up with Brazil, which held its first round of presidential elections on Sunday.

India's foreign exchange reserves have dropped by $18.34 billion in a single week, and actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
